Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmanal St., Diliman, Quezon City OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL OPINION NO. 7 S. eou..— 12 February 2009 MR. CARLITO T. TARIMAN No. IO Faisal St., Filinvest II Quezon City Dear Mr. Tariman: This refers to your letter seeking clarification on the legal issue involved relative to the establishment of your gas refilling station in Virac, Catanduanes. You stated that pursuant to Municipal Ordinance No. 2006-09, some necessary permits for the operation of your gas refilling station were issued. However, said Ordinance was declared by the RTC, Branch 43 of Virac, Catanduanes, as null and void, which decision was affirmed by the Court of Appeals 5th Division. There being no more court action that followed, said decision became final. The court decision likewise directed to recall all permits, licenses and any other form of authorization issued pursuant to the declared invalid Municipal Ordinance. Lately, you applied before the Sangguniang Bayan for a reclassification of two (2) lots, including the same land where your completed gas refilling station is located. On 19 January 2009, Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 was passed and approved reclassifying the area where your refilling gas station is located from residential to commercial. Meantime, pursuant to the provisions of the Local Government Code, said Ordinance was forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review, which up to the present, remains pending thereat. In view of the foregoing representations, you would now like to be clarified on whether or not you can now immediately open and operate your gas refilling station upon issuance by the Mayor of the necessary business permit to operate despite the pendency of the review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Catanduanes of Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01. This request for clarification was impelled by your apprehension of the effect of Section 47 of the Revised

-2- Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of the Municipality of Virac, which provides that: "SEC. 47. Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance.- Changes in the Zoning Ordinance as a result of the view by the Local Zoning Review Committee shaZZ be treated as an amendment, provided that any amendment to the Zoning Ordinance or provisions thereof shan be subject to public hearing and review etuZuation of the Local Zoning Review Committee and shaZZ be carried out through a resolution of three fourths tote of the Sangguniang Bayan. Said Amendments shall take effect only after approval and authentication by the Sangguniang PanZaZawigan. Since Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 can be categorized as amendments to the Revised Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of that municipality, you are now in a quandary as to whether or not Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 is already effective in view also of Section 3 thereof, which provides that: "Effectivity.- This Ordinance shaU take effect upon approznL Before dwelling on the specific provisions of the two (2) municipal ordinances that you mentioned, allow us first to discuss the general provisions found in the Local Govemment Code pertaining to the power of review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan over municipal ordinances and the effectivity thereof pending review. Under Section 56 of the Local Government Code, municipal ordinances are required to be forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan is required to render its findings on review within thirty (30) days after submission of such ordinance, otherwise, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and, therefore, valid. Along this line, it is also relevant to point out Section 58 of the Local Government Code, which provides that any attempt to enforce any ordinance after the disapproval tnereof, shall be sufficient ground for the suspension or dismissal of the official or employee concerned. Also related is Section 59 of the same Code, which, as to the effectivity of ordinances, provides that unless otherwise stated in the ordinance, the said ordinance shall take effect after ten (10) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. With respect to ordinances with penal sanctions, publication of the same in a newspaper of general circulation within

-3- the province where the local legislative body belongs is further required. Taken together, the privotal issue now would be, i.e., whether or not a Municipal Ordinance can already be effective and implemented while the same is pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. We answer in the affirmative. It is noted that per Section 59 of the Local Government Code, the local legislative body which passed the ordinance can expressly state therein the effectivity date of the said ordinance and in the absence of any effectivity time thereof, the same shall take effect after ten (10) days from the required posting. Accordingly, upon the arrival of the effectivity date as so stated in the ordinance and posting requirement already complied with prior to such arrival of the period, the ordinance shall, as a matter of course, be already given legal effect and implemented even if the same is still pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. However, pursuant to Section 58 of the same Code, once advised by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the disapproval of the said municipal ordinance, the Local Chief Executive of the municipality concerned shall immediately stop to enforce the disapproved municipal ordinance. At this point, it is unfortunate that the Local Government Code failed to provide an administrative remedy which the Municipal Mayor can avail of in such a situation. However, we believe that judicial reliefs may be availed of by filing the appropriate petition in the proper RTC and at the same time seek injunction so that the effectivity of the disapproval by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan will be in the meantime stayed. Going now to the specific provisions of the two (2) municipal ordinances, your apprehension anchors on the fact that Section 47 of the Revised Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance provides that any amendments thereto shall take effect only after approval and authentication by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. On the other hand, Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 provides that the same shall take effect upon approval. It is not quite clear, however, whose approval is being referred to. Nonetheless, in the absence of any specific reference, it can be safely presumed that the "approval" referred to in Section 3 of Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 is the approval by the Municipal Mayor of the enacted ordinance pursuant to Section 54 of the Local Government Code. In relation thereto, it may become worth discussing the principle of the exercise of the local Sanggunians of their local legislative powers. Under the Constitution, the power to legislate is conferred unto the legislative branch which is headed by Congress. However, Congress, through Section 48 of the Local Government Code, delegated the exercise of the power of local legislation to the Sanggunians of the local government units at all levels. Because of this

-4- principle, the Supreme Court, in a lot of jurisprudence, consistently held that since Sanggunians are merely exercising delegated legislative powers, the local ordinances, which are the product of local legislation by the Sanggunians, must always be consistent with national laws passed by Congress. It is in this light that we see some legal infirmity on the provision of Section 47 of the Revised Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance providing that amendments thereto shall take effect only after approval and authentication by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. The reason for this conclusion is the fact that Section 59 of the Local Government Code empowers the Sanggunian to expressly provide in its enacted ordinance an effectivity date thereof. The specific portion discussed in Section 47 of the Revised Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of that municipality cannot rise over and above the provisions of Section 59 of the Local Government Code. Accordingly, when the legislative wisdom of the Sangguniang Bayan is to make Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 effective upon approval thereof, such legislative wisdom should be respected as the determination of its effectivity was made pursuant to Section 59 of the Local Government Code. Considering the foregoing discussion, it is clear that Municipal Ordinance No. 2009-01 can already be implemented on the effectivity date provided therein even if the same is still pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. In reply, therefore, to your specific query, we are of the view that upon issuance by the Municipal Mayor of the necessary permits to operate your gas refilling station, then you can immediately open and operate the same. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. ANADE O Undersecreta V OASLAHRD:43/La cc: Director Blandino M. Maceda DILG Regional Office No. 05 Legazpi City
